lessons.content: A linear equation is like a balanced scale. Whatever operation you apply to one side (add, subtract, multiply, divide), you must apply the exact same operation to the other side.
When variable terms appear on both sides of the equation, transpose variable terms to one side and numeric constants to the other side by applying inverse operations.
Rational numbers can be added, subtracted, multiplied and divided. Remember that before adding or subtracting, fractions must have a common denominator.
Squaring a number means multiplying the number by itself (e.g. 7² = 7 × 7 = 49). It is NOT multiplying by 2.
Exponent rules: When multiplying powers with the same base, add their exponents: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n).
Standard algebraic identities: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b², and (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b².
A percentage represents parts out of 100. Always express p% as p/100 before computing.
Transposition Rule: When a term crosses the equal sign '=', its sign flips. Addition becomes subtraction (+ becomes -), and subtraction becomes addition (- becomes +).
Inverse Operations: If a number is added (e.g. x + 5), subtract 5. If a number is multiplied (e.g. 5x), divide by 5.
Prerequisite Bridge (Class 6 Integers): When subtracting a larger positive integer from a smaller one, the result is negative (e.g. 3 - 7 = -4). Move left on the number line.
Variable Transposition: A variable term like 3x follows the same rules as numbers. Moving +3x across '=' requires subtracting 3x on both sides.
Fraction Denominators: Denominators represent the size of parts and must never be added directly. Convert fractions to a common denominator first, then add only the numerators.
Fraction Division: Keep the first fraction, change '÷' to '×', and invert the second fraction (turn it upside down into its reciprocal).
Powers vs Multiplication: n² means n × n. For example, 7² is 7 × 7 = 49, whereas 7 × 2 = 14. Do not confuse squaring with doubling.
Exponent Addition: When multiplying identical bases (a^m × a^n), exponents ADD (m + n). Exponents multiply only when a power is raised to another power (a^m)^n = a^(m×n).
Identity Middle Term: (a + b)² is (a + b)(a + b) = a² + ab + ba + b² = a² + 2ab + b². Never omit the middle term 2ab.
Percentage Value: % means 'divided by 100'. 15% is 15/100 = 0.15. Never treat 15% as 15 units.

[ड्राफ्ट - असमीक्षित] चर को अलग करना: पहले जोड़/घटाव को हटाएं, फिर गुणा/भाग को।

[ड्राफ्ट - असमीक्षित] प्रतिशत गणना: किसी संख्या का X% = (X / 100) × संख्या।
